title: ESX type VII secretion
dek: Five ESX loci. ESX-1 is the virulence/RD1 object (ESAT-6/CFP-10). ESX-3 handles iron. ESX-5 is essential and PPE-heavy. IGRA antigens are an ESX-1 side effect.
story: Mycobacteria use type VII secretion systems (ESX-1 through ESX-5 in Mtb). Each locus encodes a membrane complex plus small Esx substrates. ESX-1 secretes EsxA (ESAT-6) and EsxB (CFP-10), among others, and is required for phagosomal membrane damage and full virulence.

Region of difference 1 (RD1) covers a chunk of ESX-1. It is deleted in BCG and M. microti, which is why those organisms are attenuated and why ESAT-6/CFP-10 IGRAs can separate Mtb infection from BCG vaccination (with caveats for some NTM).

ESX-3 is tied to mycobactin iron acquisition and is essential in Mtb. ESX-5 secretes many PPE/PE proteins and is essential. ESX-2 and ESX-4 are the quieter siblings; ESX-4 is the evolutionary elder. Locus name is not interchangeable with “the secretion system that makes granulomas.”
deep: esxA/esxB are co-secreted as a heterodimer; calling one without the partner in a deletion analysis is incomplete.
EspACD and the EspB substrate are part of the ESX-1 apparatus. Loss-of-function in accessory genes can phenocopy RD1 without a tidy RD1 deletion.
IGRA peptides are a short ESAT-6/CFP-10 (and TB7.7 in QFT-Plus) list. They are not a virulence assay and they are not DST.
Do not treat an ESX-1 frameshift in a clinical WGS as “this isolate is BCG” without the rest of the RD barcode — clinical Mtb can lose bits; BCG has a specific deletion history.

visual.caption: ESX-1 is the RD1/IGRA/virulence axis. ESX-3 is iron. ESX-5 is essential PPE secretion. BCG is an RD1 deletion, not a different genus.

example.title: Positive TST, negative IGRA after BCG
example.setup: Adult vaccinated with BCG in childhood, TST 12 mm, QFT-Plus negative, no TB exposure, normal CXR.

steps.title: Antigen difference
steps.body: TST is PPD, which includes BCG-shared proteins. QFT uses ESAT-6/CFP-10 that BCG lacks because of RD1.

steps.title: This is not sterility
steps.body: A negative IGRA does not prove absence of infection; a positive TST here is likely BCG memory, not proof of LTBI.

steps.title: Decision
steps.body: In a low-risk adult, most programmes would not treat LTBI on TST alone in this pattern. Know your national overlay.

example.takeaway: IGRA antigens are ESX-1 peptides. BCG deleted the locus.

check.answer: RD1 / ESX-1 deletion removing ESAT-6 and CFP-10 secretion
check.why: pncA explains PZA-R in M. bovis, not IGRA antigens.

check.prompt: Mtb encodes ESX-1 through ESX-5. How many paralogous type VII loci is that, and which is the RD1 virulence locus?
choices: One locus duplicated five times in the RRDR
check.why: ESX-3 is iron; ESX-5 is PPE; ESX-1 is RD1.
